title: Bath curse tablets — divine retribution, private prayer, or restitution ritual?
description: Tests how material evidence and interpreted ritual intent are linked without treating reconstructed motive as direct fact.

support: The tablets are inscribed private prayers from people reporting losses or injustices and asking Sulis Minerva for redress or revenge.
counterevidence: The modern label curse tablet can over-compress distinct motives such as restitution, punishment, prayer, and ritualized complaint.
edges.notes: This edge links a material corpus to competing descriptions of ritual intent; it does not assert that every tablet has the same purpose.
